# Best home backup power stations under $1,000

**Best overall: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2, $899**
- It has 2,074 Wh, a 2,600 W inverter, LiFePO4 cells rated for 6,000+ cycles, and a UPS switchover of 15 ms or less. That's roughly a day or two of fridge, router and lights.
- Its one limit is that it can't be expanded.
- Dealectric lists a code, AFF5OFF, that brought it to $854.05 when they tested it on 10/24.
- [Buy the Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2)
- Sources: [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-home-backup-power-stations-under-1000-2026-reviews-price-battery-capacity), [Outage Outfitter](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/)
- Prices conflict across sources. An Oct 7 [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup) update said Bluetti ended a promo and listed it at $1,199, while the Oct 19 and Oct 24 pages show $899. Check the cart price before you buy.

**Best if you want to expand later: Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2, about $900**
- It has 2,048 Wh, 2,400 W and a true UPS function, and it takes add-on batteries. Outage Authority says a BP2000 pack doubles capacity to 4 kWh, and it also has a TT-30 RV outlet.
- I didn't get a direct purchase link in the results. It is sold on Amazon, and the [Outage Outfitter page](https://outageoutfitter.com/best/under-1000/) has the Amazon link.
- Sources: [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/), [Outage Authority](https://outageauthority.com/roundups/best-power-station-home-backup)
- Another expandable option is the [BLUETTI AC200L](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac200l) at $899. It expands to 8,192 Wh, but it is rated for fewer cycles (3,000+).

**Best value for short outages: BLUETTI AC180, $499**
- It has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W, which works out to about 13 hours of fridge, CPAP and router by Outage Authority's math. It weighs 35.3 lb and isn't expandable.
- Dealectric's code AFF5OFF brought it to $474.05.
- [Buy the AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

**Lightest 1 kWh option: Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, about $489**
- It's the lightest in its class at 23.8 lb, but it has 1,500 W output, only 400 W solar input and no expansion.
- The $489 price is from a third-party retailer, Outbound Power. Jackery's own store is $559.
- Source: [Outage Authority review](https://outageauthority.com/reviews/jackery-explorer-1000-v2)

**Cheapest per watt-hour: Anker SOLIX F1500, $599.99**
- It has 1,536 Wh and 600 W solar input, and Compare Power Stations flags the price as unusually low. I found no hands-on review in these results, so treat it as a spec-and-price pick.
- Source: [Compare Power Stations](https://comparepowerstations.com/best/best-under-1000/)

**How to choose**
- For a typical outage of a fridge, router and CPAP, 2 kWh (the Elite 200 V2 or C2000 Gen 2) covers about a day. A 1 kWh unit covers about 12 hours.
- Pick the C2000 Gen 2 if you might want more capacity later. Otherwise the Elite 200 V2 has the longer cycle life.
- If you need a window AC, well pump or other big loads, these units won't be enough.

Most of these sites say they haven't tested the units themselves and rely on maker specs. The links are affiliate links, and prices change often.
